title: Download GlassFolio for your computer
intro: A real desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux: install it, open it, and your portfolio lives in its own window. No Docker, no terminal, and your data stays on your machine, encrypted.

hero.headingAny: GlassFolio for Mac, Windows and Linux
hero.anySpec: Pick your system to get the installer.
hero.mobileNote: GlassFolio installs on a computer. Open this page on your Mac, Windows PC or Linux machine, or pick a system below.
hero.switchToIntel: Mac with an Intel chip? Download the Intel version.

comingSoon.body: The desktop app is built and tested; the first installers are about to be published on GitHub. Until then you can run GlassFolio with Docker, or try the cloud version.

all.title: All systems and versions
all.subtitle: macOS, Windows and Linux, with the steps for the first launch

mac.name: macOS
mac.hint: Not sure which one? Apple menu > About This Mac: if the chip starts with “Apple M”, pick Apple Silicon; otherwise pick Intel.

win.name: Windows
win.hint: The installer sets GlassFolio up for your account only: no administrator rights needed.

linux.name: Linux
linux.hint: The AppImage runs on most distributions and updates itself. The .deb package is for Debian and Ubuntu and is updated from the download page.

window.title: Its own window
window.body: GlassFolio opens like any other app, with no browser tab and no address to remember.

local.title: Your data stays here
local.body: Your portfolio is encrypted with your master password and saved on your computer. Nothing leaves it unless you connect a service yourself.

updates.title: Updates, with your say
updates.body: GlassFolio tells you when a new version is out and installs it when you click, then restarts. You can turn the check off.

ai.title: Ready for your AI tools
ai.body: The MCP bridge works as in the Docker edition, so Claude, Cursor and others can read your portfolio once you allow it.

firstLaunch.title: The first time you open it
firstLaunch.intro: GlassFolio is free and open source, and it is not signed with a paid developer certificate yet. Your system therefore asks you to confirm the first launch. This is expected; here is how, once.

mac.title: On a Mac

steps.s1: Open the .dmg and drag GlassFolio into Applications.
steps.s2: Open GlassFolio from Applications. macOS says it cannot verify the app: close that message.
steps.s3: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, click “Open Anyway” next to GlassFolio and confirm. On macOS 14 and earlier, right-click the app and choose Open instead.

mac.after: Later launches, and updates installed from inside the app, open normally.

steps.s1: Run the installer. If “Windows protected your PC” appears, click “More info”.
steps.s2: Click “Run anyway”, then follow the installer.

steps.s1: AppImage: make it executable (chmod +x GlassFolio-linux-x64.AppImage), then run it.
steps.s2: Debian or Ubuntu: sudo apt install ./GlassFolio-linux-x64.deb

ways.title: Three ways to use GlassFolio
ways.intro: The same app, the same encryption and the same features. Choose where it runs, and switch whenever you like.

desktop.title: Desktop app
desktop.body: The simplest way to keep everything on your computer: install it like any other app.

points.p1: Its own window, with no Docker and no terminal
points.p2: Your data stays on your computer, encrypted
points.p3: New versions offered inside the app

desktop.note: On a Mac, the app unlocks with your master password. Touch ID, passkeys and the autofill of your password manager work in the browser versions (Docker and cloud).

docker.title: Docker
docker.body: Run GlassFolio as a container on your computer or on a home server, and open it in your browser. The same local, encrypted vault.
docker.note: It opens in your browser, so Touch ID, passkeys and your password manager work like on any website.

cloud.title: Cloud version
cloud.body: Nothing to install: create a free account and use GlassFolio from any browser, with your data end-to-end encrypted.
cloud.note: It runs in your browser too, and follows you on all your devices.

updates.title: How updates work
updates.body: When GlassFolio starts, and every few hours after, it asks GitHub for the latest release. GitHub therefore sees your IP address, like for any web request; nothing about you or your data is sent. The update information is signed, and every download is checked against its fingerprint before anything is installed. If a new version exists, you choose: update now, or later. You can turn the check off in Settings.

verify.title: Check what you download
verify.body: Each release lists the SHA-256 fingerprint of every installer. Compare it with the one of your download if you want to be sure.
